title: Implement a Service Health Check Mechanism with Incremental Rollout
description: The StageStream Orchestrator is responsible for deploying and managing a fleet of services. A critical missing feature is a health check mechanism to ensure that deployed services are actually operational. This task involves implementing this feature incrementally over several development sessions. The goal is to add a health status to each managed service and create a background process within the orchestrator to periodically update this status via a network check.

project_spec.name: StageStream Orchestrator
project_spec.description:
StageStream Orchestrator is a medium-scale, C-based network control plane designed for modern live-entertainment venues (concert halls, e-sports arenas, theme-park attractions). It exposes a real-time API that lets light shows, audio mixers, projection systems and audience-interaction mobile apps all plug into the same managed network while guaranteeing uptime, balanced traffic and detailed performance insights.

Built around the Model-View-Controller paradigm, StageStream encapsulates its device registry, show presets and historic performance logs in the Model layer; dispatches all incoming network events (OSC, MIDI-over-IP, WebSocket commands from operator tablets, REST calls from DevOps pipelines) through an Event-Driven Controller layer that chains responsibility modules (authentication → rate-limiting → command routing); and finally renders system state to a variety of Views such as a GTK+ desktop dashboard, a lightweight web panel and a Prometheus metrics endpoint.

The system bakes in enterprise-grade networking concerns—system_monitoring, log_aggregation, performance_metrics, backup_recovery, deployment_automation and load_balancing—while still keeping the focus squarely on showtime excitement: operators can schedule “scene” commands that ripple through a service mesh of micro-daemons controlling lasers, pyrotechnics and media servers, all without dropping frames or audio beats.
dependencies: libevent / libuv – high-performance, non-blocking event loop (Controller)
ZeroMQ – service mesh message bus (Command_Pattern, Service_Mesh)
cJSON – fast JSON (de)serialization for network payloads
zlog – structured log_aggregation with runtime log levels
libarchive – incremental backup_recovery of configuration snapshots
OpenSSL – TLS for secure operator/control traffic
libmicrohttpd – embedded HTTP server for web View & deployment_automation hooks
systemd-sd-journal – native system_monitoring integration on Linux
HAProxy cfg generator – automated load_balancing between micro-daemons
